lineage: Mario ESXi encryptor shares code with leaked Babuk source
summary: RansomHouse (tracked by Unit 42 as Jolly Scorpius) is a RaaS/double-extortion operation active since December 2021 with 120+ leak-site victims across healthcare, finance, transportation and government. Affiliates gain access via spear-phishing or exploitation of vulnerable systems, use third-party tooling for recon and lateral movement, exfiltrate with compression and file-transfer utilities, then deploy the MrAgent management binary on VMware ESXi hypervisors to automate mass deployment of the Mario encryptor. Unit 42 reported a multi-layer encryption upgrade to Mario in December 2025.
uniqueTraits: MrAgent: purpose-built ESXi deployment agent with persistent C2, host profiling via esxcli and remote 'Run'/'Exec' commands
MrAgent disables the ESXi firewall (esxcli network firewall set --enabled false), changes the root password and stops vpxa to cut vCenter management
Changes the ESXi DCUI welcome message as part of the deployment
Mario encryptor targets VM disks and Veeam backup files (.vmdk, .vmem, .vmsn, .vbk, .vbm) to defeat recovery; .emario extension
Hypervisor-first impact: encrypts many VMs at once rather than individual Windows hosts

sources.title: From Linear to Complex: An Upgrade in RansomHouse Encryption

chain.procedure: Affiliates gain initial access through spear-phishing and other social engineering.

atomics.note: [T1566.001] Macro-enabled phishing attachment download; the exact RansomHouse lure format is not published.

chain.procedure: Affiliates exploit vulnerable systems in the victim environment, including zero-day and n-day exploits.
chain.noAtomicReason: No local Atomic Red Team test performs public-facing application exploitation; specific CVEs are not named in reporting.

chain.procedure: Third-party tools and frameworks are used to map the environment and locate hypervisors and valuable data.

atomics.note: [T1046] Nmap port scan as representative third-party network mapping.
[T1018] SoftPerfect NetScan remote host enumeration.

chain.procedure: Affiliates escalate privileges and move laterally using third-party tooling before reaching the hypervisors (specific protocols not detailed).

atomics.note: [T1021.001] RDP to remote host as a common lateral movement path.
[T1021.002] Admin share mapping as an alternative lateral movement path.

chain.techniqueName: Archive Collected Data: Archive via Utility
chain.procedure: Stolen data is compressed with file compression utilities prior to exfiltration.

atomics.testName: Compress Data and lock with password for Exfiltration with 7zip
atomics.note: [T1560.001] Password-protected 7-Zip archive for exfiltration.

atomics.testName: Compress Data for Exfiltration With Rar
atomics.note: [T1560.001] RAR compression for exfiltration.

chain.procedure: File transfer utilities send data to attacker-controlled servers (Trellix also notes CDN-based exfiltration infrastructure).

atomics.testName: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol - FTP - Rclone
atomics.note: [T1048.003] Rclone over FTP to an external server.

atomics.testName: Exfiltrate data HTTPS using curl windows
atomics.note: [T1048.002] HTTPS exfiltration with curl.

chain.procedure: MrAgent is deployed on ESXi hosts, keeps a persistent connection to C2, pulls configuration and later downloads the Mario encryptor directly onto the hypervisor.

atomics.note: [T1105] curl download of a remote payload, representative of MrAgent pulling the encryptor.

chain.procedure: MrAgent profiles the hypervisor: uname -a, esxcli --formatter=csv network nic list (MAC) and esxcli network ip interface ipv4 get (IP).

atomics.note: [T1082] ESXi VM/host discovery using ESXCLI.
[T1082] ESXi system information discovery (Darkside-style esxcli usage).

chain.procedure: Mario searches datastores for VM and backup files by extension (.vmdk, .vmem, .vmsd, .vmsn, .vswp, .ova, .ovf, .vbk, .vbm, .vib).

atomics.testName: ESXi - Enumerate VMDKs available on an ESXi Host
atomics.note: [T1083] Enumerates VMDKs available on an ESXi host.

chain.techniqueName: Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify System Firewall
chain.procedure: MrAgent disables the ESXi firewall with esxcli network firewall set --enabled false.

atomics.note: [T1686] ESXi firewall disabled via esxcli.

atomics.testName: ESXi - Set Firewall to PASS Traffic
atomics.note: [T1686] ESXi firewall set to pass traffic.

chain.procedure: The MrAgent 'Exec' instruction changes the ESXi root password to lock administrators out during deployment.

atomics.note: [T1531] Changes a user password to remove access; Windows stand-in for the ESXi root password change.

chain.procedure: Stops vCenter remote management on the host (/etc/init.d/vpxa stop) before encryption.

atomics.note: [T1489] Service stop via net.exe; Windows analogue of stopping vpxa.

chain.procedure: MrAgent's 'Welcome' instruction changes the ESXi DCUI welcome message.

atomics.testName: ESXi - Change Welcome Message on Direct Console User Interface (DCUI)
atomics.note: [T1491.001] Changes the ESXi DCUI welcome message.

chain.procedure: Mario deliberately encrypts Veeam backup files (.vbk/.vbm) and VM snapshot/state files to prevent recovery.

atomics.note: [T1490] Deletes backup files; models loss of backup artefacts.

chain.procedure: Mario (Babuk-derived) encrypts VM disks with a multi-layer scheme (Dec 2025 upgrade), appends a 'mario' extension (e.g. .emario) and drops 'How To Restore Your Files.txt'; victims are pressured via Telegram and the leak site.

atomics.note: [T1486] Ransom-note drop simulation (non-encrypting).

atomics.testName: ESXi - vim-cmd Used to Power Off VMs
atomics.note: [T1529] vim-cmd VM power-off that precedes hypervisor-level encryption.
